opening.text: Book is up 14.7% — $1,412 on $1,231 deposited — and that is with Bitcoin sitting 37% below its October 2025 high. ZEC is the engine: $939 entry, $1,090 now, +15.0% in ten days, riding a Grayscale ZCSH ETF that pulled $463M in its first ten sessions. Privacy is the only sector in crypto trading above its Oct-2025 ATH level, up 213%. LTC +4.9% with a live ETF and a commodity classification, SOL +8.2% with Schwab distribution. Four of seven green while the total market cap fell 4.25% in a day. This is what a portfolio built on catalysts rather than beta looks like.

Numbers straight. LINK $11.27 vs $11.73 entry, -3.9% at day 15 — that trips the 14-day dead-money rule. I am overriding it, and here is the arithmetic behind the override: Coinbase named Chainlink the oracle for tokenized US stocks on Base, Schwab added LINK alongside SOL and AVAX, Bottomline is routing bank ISO-20022 messaging through CCIP. LINK printed $13.64 on Sep 7 and gave it back with the tape, not with the thesis. NEAR is the worst mark at -6.3% ($2.45 to $2.29) but its supply schedule just hit ~100% circulating, which removes the unlock overhang permanently, and Confidential Intents TVL is closing on the $70M snapshot trigger. Day 7. It stays. ADA at -3.5% is the one I cannot defend on fundamentals — it is a position with no catalyst attached.

Read the regime, not the P&L. BTC dominance 58.9% and climbing toward the 60% line that forces liquidation across this entire book. Fear & Greed 61, down from 73 a week ago — the greed is draining. Total market cap -4.25% in 24 hours and six of our seven names were red on the day. BTC must hold $77,000; analysts put the next real shelf at $52,000 if it does not. And the operational constraint is the whole story: buying power is $7.14. Not $714 — seven dollars. If a genuine capitulation wick prints next week, this account watches it happen. Full conviction, zero dry powder, is not a strategy, it is a condition.

Everyone in this room is congratulating themselves on ZEC while ignoring what it actually is: a 2,496% twelve-month move, 82nd to 7th by market cap, powered by a $212M liquidation cascade that was 75% shorts. That is not accumulation, that is a squeeze wearing an ETF costume. The contrarian read is that the crowded, obvious trade here is privacy, and the neglected one is the name nobody will defend — ADA at -3.5% with a dead catalyst calendar is exactly the profile that gets bought at the bottom of sentiment, not sold. Separately: this book is seven altcoins and no Bitcoin while dominance rises. We sold BTC on Sep 6 at +25% and SOL, LINK, NEAR have not outrun it since. The exit may have been the mistake, not the entries.
